measures.label: Overall rating
measures.definition: CMS collapses up to 46 measures into five groups, then into a single star. Two hospitals can share a rating with very different underlying profiles, so read the group counts below it before drawing a conclusion.

measures.label: Measures reported
measures.definition: How many of the measures CMS tracks this facility actually reported. Low-volume hospitals report fewer, which is a reporting artefact rather than a quality signal — it is shown so a sparse profile is never mistaken for a poor one.

measures.label: Measures better than national
measures.definition: Count of measures where this facility performed statistically better than the national rate. Compare against measures reported: 3 of 4 is not the same result as 3 of 40.

measures.label: Measures worse than national
measures.definition: Count of measures where this facility performed statistically worse than the national rate.

measures.label: Mortality measures better
measures.definition: Of the mortality measures reported, how many were better than the national rate. Risk-adjusted for how sick patients were on arrival.

measures.label: Safety measures better
measures.definition: Of the safety-of-care measures reported (infections and complications), how many were better than the national rate.

measures.label: Readmission measures better
measures.definition: Of the unplanned-readmission measures reported, how many were better than the national rate. Readmission is a proxy for whether discharge was premature, and it penalises hospitals serving patients with less support at home.
